body:
The Truth Shall Make You Free · Kente FM Radio · 2017-05-16 · Bishop Nathanyel

Opens [Jer 2](/bible/jeremiah/2) · [Matt 3](/bible/matthew/3) · [John 20](/bible/john/20) · [Acts 1](/bible/acts/1) · [Acts 5](/bible/acts/5) · [Jer 23](/bible/jeremiah/23) · [1 Pet 3](/bible/1-peter/3) · [1 Cor 10](/bible/1-corinthians/10) · [Rev 22](/bible/revelation/22) · [Acts 21](/bible/acts/21) · [Num 6](/bible/numbers/6)
## Introduction *[[0:04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BQQG5qW66cs&t=4s)]* **Host:** Today we are going to deal with the topic baptism, the understanding of baptism, and if God permits and we have time we are going to deal with prayer, what kind of prayer we have to pray to the Most High God. We have different types of baptism in the Bible: Holy Ghost baptism, baptism by immersion. Is it important that when we come to the knowledge of the truth we have to do baptism by immersion, or what do we have to do? What is the understanding? *[[0:55](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BQQG5qW66cs&t=55s)]* I'd like to start off by saying that the term Black Hebrew Israelite was first used by the white man to say that black people are not the real Israelites. That is why they use the term Black Hebrew Israelites, to imply that the real ones are white or Caucasian. So we shun away from those terms and we just use the term the Bible says, Israelites, because we are the one only true Israelites; that's who we are. The white man, as you know, he's the devil that the Bible speaks of. He's a racist; he hates all people but himself. Even the liberal ones, they smile in your face and deceive you and stab you in your back. They make up these terms, these wordings, to identify us as being false, and they hope and want everyone else to use the terms they invent. Remember the boxer Muhammad Ali: when he converted to Islam they called him a black Muslim. He said, I'm not a black Muslim, I am a Muslim. They like to do that, to make a distinction between the real and the fake; every time he tries to use an adjective to confuse our people. *[[3:42](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BQQG5qW66cs&t=222s)]* Many times I've noticed that women come in and always ask about water baptism, and a few brothers ask about water baptism. They've just gone from one religion to the next. Some of them are Roman Catholic: they had water sprinkled on them as a baby, then they became older and they got immersed in water, now they hear the truth that they're Israel and they ask again, hey, should I get baptized? Well, the other water baptisms did nothing for you. So now we want to discuss the history of water baptism. ## Scriptures Opened **[Jeremiah 2:22](/bible/jeremiah/2#v22)** *[[4:47](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BQQG5qW66cs&t=287s)]* > [22](/bible/jeremiah/2#v22) For though thou wash thee with nitre, and take thee much soap, yet thine iniquity is marked before me, saith the Lord God. - When you read in the book of Numbers, remember when the Most High called Israel before the mount (it might have been Deuteronomy or Numbers, I can't recall at this second), he said to Israel you had to wash yourself in water, I believe it was three days, before they could come up to the mountain. - So Israel from that point would use water to cleanse themselves, just like in Leviticus 15: if you had a running issue or the seed of copulation, you had to wash yourself in water and then be clean by the evening time. So the use of water was always there. - Notice what Jeremiah says: though thou wash thee with nitre (it's a cleaning solution) and take thee much soap, yet thine iniquity is marked before me. - So although we were still following the custom here of bathing and washing, God said our iniquity was still marked before him. Why? Because our minds, our spirits, is still defiled. **[Matthew 3:6-10](/bible/matthew/3#v6)** *[[6:44](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BQQG5qW66cs&t=404s)]* > [6](/bible/matthew/3#v6) And were baptized of him in Jordan, confessing their sins. > > [7](/bible/matthew/3#v7) But when he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees come to his baptism, he said unto them, O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come? > > [8](/bible/matthew/3#v8) Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance: > > [9](/bible/matthew/3#v9) And think not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham. > > [10](/bible/matthew/3#v10) And now also the axe is laid unto the root of the trees: therefore every tree which bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire. - Notice the next three words: confessing their sins. The white man has perverted baptism today. When people get baptized today (and I've been baptized many times in the water), we never confessed our sins; we never understood what sin is. - In America there's people who use crack, go to church, get baptized in water, then leave the church and use crack again the same day. Women who are adulteresses and harlots will commit adultery on Saturday, go to church on Sunday, get baptized, and then commit adultery and fornication Sunday night with the pastor. This wickedness must end. Nobody confesses their sin. - Notice what he calls the scribes, the Pharisees: O generation of vipers. Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance: John was letting them know you have to bring forth works that prove you've repented. The works is God's commandments. I'm going to say it again: the works is God's commandments. - It is not saying things like 'God bless you', 'I love you'. Those are terms that Christians always use, but in their heart they are still wicked, because they're bearing false witness, they're worshipping a false god, they're breaking the Sabbath day, they're committing adultery. The word meet means good for repentance. So when the people got baptized in water, they had to show their works by keeping God's commandments. - The scribes, the Pharisees and the Sadducees had a doctrine that said we are Abraham's seed, so therefore we're good with God. John says no: just because you're Abraham's seed does not absolve you from your sin, cause God can raise up children to Abraham from rocks. Talking to the brothers in Nigeria, some are under the misconception that because they know that they're Israelites, that's all they need. That's false; that is the same thing John dealt with here in verse 9. - And now also the axe is laid unto the root of the trees: every child of Abraham that does not bring forth good fruit is the tree that has to be cut down. The tree represents humans, the Israelites. John was using the metaphor, the similitude, of men as trees. Precepts: - **[Psalms 1:1-3](/bible/psalms/1#v1)** > [1](/bible/psalms/1#v1) Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful. > > [2](/bible/psalms/1#v2) But his delight is in the law of the Lord; and in his law doth he meditate day and night. > > [3](/bible/psalms/1#v3) And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season; his leaf also shall not wither; and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper. A precept regarding trees being people. Remember sin means breaking God's commandments. He that has delight in God's law is like a tree planted by the rivers of living water; you see the metaphor. **[John 20:21-23](/bible/john/20#v21)** *[[12:35](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BQQG5qW66cs&t=755s)]* > [21](/bible/john/20#v21) Then said Jesus to them again, Peace be unto you: as my Father hath sent me, even so send I you. > > [22](/bible/john/20#v22) And when he had said this, he breathed on them, and saith unto them, Receive ye the Holy Ghost: > > [23](/bible/john/20#v23) Whose soever sins ye remit, they are remitted unto them; and whose soever sins ye retain, they are retained. - Number one, the scriptural understanding. Notice it says he breathed on them and said, Receive ye the Holy Ghost. - Whosoever sins ye remit, they are remitted, and whosoever sins ye retain, they are retained: this Holy Ghost is talking about a scriptural understanding, so that you can forgive or retain sin. - Now watch the difference between this and Acts 1. **[Acts 1:5-8](/bible/acts/1#v5)** *[[13:28](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BQQG5qW66cs&t=808s)]* > [5](/bible/acts/1#v5) For John truly baptized with water; but ye shall be baptized with the Holy Ghost not many days hence. > > [6](/bible/acts/1#v6) When they therefore were come together, they asked of him, saying, Lord, wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel? > > [7](/bible/acts/1#v7) And he said unto them, It is not for you to know the times or the seasons, which the Father hath put in his own power. > > [8](/bible/acts/1#v8) But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth. - Compare Acts 1 verse 8 with John 20. In John 20 Christ breathed on them and said, Receive the Holy Ghost. Now in Acts 1 he says wait until you receive the Holy Ghost, which is power. - Notice in Acts 1 the Holy Ghost is used in context of spiritual power, which was different than John 20 when he breathed on them and said, Receive ye the Holy Ghost. - He's giving you two understandings of the use of the term Holy Ghost: one is power, the other is talking about a scriptural understanding so that you can forgive or retain sin. This is what most people don't understand, the difference in the term the Holy Ghost. - **Host:** You said that the power means giving them the power to retain sin? - Yes, but also remember from Acts 1 they was able to do miracles: they raised the dead, they healed the sick. So that was a level of power; that's why verse 8, But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you. **[Acts 5:15-16](/bible/acts/5#v15)** *[[16:43](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BQQG5qW66cs&t=1003s)]* > [15](/bible/acts/5#v15) Insomuch that they brought forth the sick into the streets, and laid them on beds and couches, that at the least the shadow of Peter passing by might overshadow some of them. > > [16](/bible/acts/5#v16) There came also a multitude out of the cities round about unto Jerusalem, bringing sick folks, and them which were vexed with unclean spirits: and they were healed every one. - **Host:** Do you believe in miracle, the IUIC, Israel United in Christ? Do you now believe in the power and the miracles of God? - God does miracles, but listen good to what I'm about to say. This is the misconception that Christianity has forced on the people: all the prophets did not have spiritual power. I'm going to say it again: all the prophets did not have spiritual power. The ones who had spiritual power, you had Moses of course, Elijah, Elisha, Christ and the twelve, John the Baptist, who was the greatest; Christ said he was great. - Do you see the difference? Peter's shadow could heal them. When you go to James (remember James was one of the twelve), he said anoint with oil and pray; that's different. We do that today, properly: we can anoint with oil and pray that the Lord heal the sick. That level of power, it was faded; it was not meant for all times. - **Host:** So in IUIC you actually anoint the sick and you pray? Yes, that is what we do. We tell the people, confess your sins before the Lord, and we ask the Father to forgive the brother or sister of their sin, so that they can be healed. - **Host:** Do you also accept when people have spiritual revelation, especially concerning dreams? In the book of Joel the young men shall see visions, the old men shall prophesy, so in the church when people started seeing things and dreams it become part of the doctrine of the church. We listen once in a while, but we don't entertain it to make a doctrine of it. - In the book of Joel and in Acts where it says your sons and daughters shall dream dreams, see visions (I'm paraphrasing), these are men and women keeping God's commandments as Israelites, and their dreams and visions will coincide with scripture. In Christianity you have these rebellious, pork-eating, idol-worshipping, false-holiday-keeping people, Baptist people, Pentecostal, Jehovah, saying 'oh, I had a dream', and the whole church listens to this foolishness. It is outside of scripture. You have a … rebellious woman worshipping the white man as God saying this is a fulfillment of Joel. No, it's not; that is an abomination, what you're doing, with the pork chop in your mouth, eating bush meat on the side. Get out of here with that. This is why we don't run away with these people in their dream. **[Matthew 3:11-12](/bible/matthew/3#v11)** *[[21:39](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BQQG5qW66cs&t=1299s)]* > [11](/bible/matthew/3#v11) I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance: but he that cometh after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to bear: he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost, and with fire: > > [12](/bible/matthew/3#v12) Whose fan is in his hand, and he will throughly purge his floor, and gather his wheat into the garner; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire. - The fan is an instrument used to blow fire to make it burn more. So whose fan is in his hand: this verse is talking about the thermonuclear destruction that's going to hit the earth when the Lord returns. - He will throughly purge his floor and gather his wheat into the garner: that means save the elect of Israel who keep the commandments. That's what the wheat is, those that follow the word. - But he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire: that means kill them, burn them up. **[Jeremiah 23:25-28](/bible/jeremiah/23#v25)** *[[23:45](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BQQG5qW66cs&t=1425s)]* > [25](/bible/jeremiah/23#v25) I have heard what the prophets said, that prophesy lies in my name, saying, I have dreamed, I have dreamed. > > [26](/bible/jeremiah/23#v26) How long shall this be in the heart of the prophets that prophesy lies? yea, they are prophets of the deceit of their own heart; > > [27](/bible/jeremiah/23#v27) Which think to cause my people to forget my name by their dreams which they tell every man to his neighbour, as their fathers have forgotten my name for Baal. > > [28](/bible/jeremiah/23#v28) The prophet that hath a dream, let him tell a dream; and he that hath my word, let him speak my word faithfully. What is the chaff to the wheat? saith the Lord. - Many people will ask, well, what does it mean by the wheat and the chaff? Let's look at Jeremiah 23 to explain the wheat and the chaff. Start at 25 and read down, so we can get the full 28. - I have dreamed, I have dreamed: that's like Luther King said, I have a dream, I have a dream. He's very famous for that. - They are prophets of the deceit of their own heart. **[1 Peter 3:21](/bible/1-peter/3#v21)** *[[24:59](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BQQG5qW66cs&t=1499s)]* > [21](/bible/1-peter/3#v21) The like figure whereunto even baptism doth also now save us (not the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but the answer of a good conscience toward God,) by the resurrection of Jesus Christ: - Peter says water is not going to save you; that is not the baptism that saves you. Look at the next part: but the answer of a good conscience toward God. - What gives you a good conscience toward God? **Host:** By observing the laws. That's it. That's what Peter is revealing to all of us: that is the baptism that saves us, the answer of a good conscience toward God, which means keeping the commandments. - Water has no power; water baptism cannot save you. It was a custom that the Israelites did from the time of Moses all the way up until John. - This is why when Christ came he was not dipping nobody in water. Christ said you're clean through the word, I'm telling you, you're clean through the word that I'm teaching you. **[1 Corinthians 10:1-2](/bible/1-corinthians/10#v1)** *[[25:58](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BQQG5qW66cs&t=1558s)]* > [1](/bible/1-corinthians/10#v1) Moreover, brethren, I would not that ye should be ignorant, how that all our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea; > > [2](/bible/1-corinthians/10#v2) And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea; - So was Moses doing water baptism? What baptism did Moses do for all Israel? He was teaching them the law; that's what he was doing, teaching us the law. That was the baptism Moses did. He was not dipping hundreds of thousands of people. - I want all your listeners to understand: many of them have been baptized in water two, three, some four times, and they have not changed. - The true baptism is having a good conscience toward God by keeping the commandments, believing the resurrection of Jesus Christ. That is the true baptism. **[Revelation 22:14](/bible/revelation/22#v14)** *[[26:56](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BQQG5qW66cs&t=1616s)]* > [14](/bible/revelation/22#v14) Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life, and may enter in through the gates into the city. - He didn't say blessed are they that get water baptized, that you may enter through the gates of the city. No, he said blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life and may enter in through the gates into the city. - What every Christian disavows: they reject it, they say no, no, water, water is the key. Water is not the key. - **Host:** You and I, we bathe every day; we wash the filth of the flesh every day. We use soaps, and sometimes things which have a very sweet aroma, the fragrance, but yet if we don't practice the law it means nothing. Precepts: - **[Psalms 51:7](/bible/psalms/51#v7)** > [7](/bible/psalms/51#v7) Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean: wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow. **Host:** There's a chapter in the book of Psalms, it says Purge me with hyssop and I shall be whiter than snow. That was a cleansing solution, and I was trying to find the meaning of hyssop: I found out it to be a plant; it has a medicinal … that actually fights against fungal.
Reading from a definition of hyssop *[[28:55](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BQQG5qW66cs&t=1735s)]* > Hyssop … a herbaceous plant of the genus Hyssopus. - It's a plant, used in medicine and cleansing. Purge me with hyssop, the Bible records, and I will be clean. - That's correct, it is a plant. That's what they use, and they would cleanse themselves with it. So remember, that was symbolic.
**[Acts 21:21-22](/bible/acts/21#v21)** *[[29:52](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BQQG5qW66cs&t=1792s)]* > [21](/bible/acts/21#v21) And they are informed of thee, that thou teachest all the Jews which are among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, saying that they ought not to circumcise their children, neither to walk after the customs. > > [22](/bible/acts/21#v22) What is it therefore? the multitude must needs come together: for they will hear that thou art come. - This was an accusation against the apostle Paul. But watch what they say to him; this is what James is telling him. - James was telling Paul: listen, there's an accusation that you're telling people to reject Moses. We must all come on one accord; do this vow that we say unto you, and purify yourself with them. - That's going into the law of the Nazarite, where you took a temporary vow. At the end of your vow you had to shave your hair off your head and sacrifice an animal. - Now James knew all of this was done away with in Christ, but it was something they still kept doing. This is what I want the people to see in context with water baptism, because notice it says, and purify thyself with them. **[Numbers 6:2-9,17-18](/bible/numbers/6#v2)** *[[31:59](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BQQG5qW66cs&t=1919s)]* > [2](/bible/numbers/6#v2) Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, When either man or woman shall separate themselves to vow a vow of a Nazarite, to separate themselves unto the Lord: > > [3](/bible/numbers/6#v3) He shall separate himself from wine and strong drink, and shall drink no vinegar of wine, or vinegar of strong drink, neither shall he drink any liquor of grapes, nor eat moist grapes, or dried. > > [4](/bible/numbers/6#v4) All the days of his separation shall he eat nothing that is made of the vine tree, from the kernels even to the husk. > > [5](/bible/numbers/6#v5) All the days of the vow of his separation there shall no razor come upon his head: until the days be fulfilled, in the which he separateth himself unto the Lord, he shall be holy, and shall let the locks of the hair of his head grow. > > [6](/bible/numbers/6#v6) All the days that he separateth himself unto the Lord he shall come at no dead body. > > [7](/bible/numbers/6#v7) He shall not make himself unclean for his father, or for his mother, for his brother, or for his sister, when they die: because the consecration of his God is upon his head. > > [8](/bible/numbers/6#v8) All the days of his separation he is holy unto the Lord. > > [9](/bible/numbers/6#v9) And if any man die very suddenly by him, and he hath defiled the head of his consecration; then he shall shave his head in the day of his cleansing, on the seventh day shall he shave it. > > [17](/bible/numbers/6#v17) And he shall offer the ram for a sacrifice of peace offerings unto the Lord, with the basket of unleavened bread: the priest shall offer also his meat offering, and his drink offering. > > [18](/bible/numbers/6#v18) And the Nazarite shall shave the head of his separation at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation, and shall take the hair of the head of his separation, and put it in the fire which is under the sacrifice of the peace offerings. - This is the vow that Paul took. - I want to get to some key points: if any man die very suddenly by him, he hath defiled the head of his consecration, and he shall shave his head in the day of his cleansing. - At the end the Nazarite offers the ram for a sacrifice of peace offering and puts the hair of the head of his separation in the fire which is under the sacrifice. So when we go back to Acts, this is the vow. This is what I wanted you to understand: they told Paul to do this. **[Acts 21:23-24](/bible/acts/21#v23)** *[[34:18](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BQQG5qW66cs&t=2058s)]* > [23](/bible/acts/21#v23) Do therefore this that we say to thee: We have four men which have a vow on them; > > [24](/bible/acts/21#v24) Them take, and purify thyself with them, and be at charges with them, that they may shave their heads: and all may know that those things, whereof they were informed concerning thee, are nothing; but that thou thyself also walkest orderly, and keepest the law. - Remember, this is after Christ has resurrected. They were still following certain things that they knew there was no power anymore, because Christ fulfilled all of that. They were still doing sacrifices during the vow of the Nazarites. Why? To keep the peace with Israel. - That's why I brought that up: to show you this is why in the book of Acts they were still doing water baptism, although Christ clearly said now you are clean through the word which I'm speaking unto you; washing of water by the word. - **Host:** All these things also has to do with the spirit of stiffneckedness. Christ said because you were very stiffnecked people, Moses allowed you to give a divorce certificate. If you're going to hold on to the water, what about these sacrifices of animals then? Why don't you hold on to that? - Christ fulfilled that. Christ said now you are clean through the words which I speak unto thee. They say no, I need water, water is the power, that is the key. That is not so. - **Host:** We believe in the physical things more than keeping the law, because it is the law that actually makes one holy. - I'll give you another example: in America black women get pregnant, then they have an abortion to kill the baby. Why don't you abstain from having sex until you get married? How about that? But no, they don't want to obey God's law; they'd rather commit adultery, fornication, then kill the baby. You simple people, how about obey the law? The scripture says obedience is better than sacrifice. ## In Closing *[[38:45](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BQQG5qW66cs&t=2325s)]* Remember, this truth is for the saints of Israel, the scattered diaspora. This is for our people, to redeem us in these last days. Let us all come together in Messiah; keep these commandments, because deliverance is near to come. ## Announcements & References - Visit the IUIC website at www.israelunite.org. - Bishop Nathanyel will mail the music CD to the host for the radio. - Next week, same time on Kente FM: Bishop Nathanyel on the topic of prayer. --- [Class Notes Index](/classes) · [Watch the full session on YouTube ↗](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BQQG5qW66cs)
